review.method: the acceptance suite re-run locally with `CS_GAME_DIR` set and a real GPU adapter (Apple M3 Pro, Metal), every `accept_f21_d_*` test selected by prefix with `--include-ignored`; this harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, and the coverage census the retail test derived over that installation with production readers (`cs_formats::interp::decode_interp`, `cs_content::scene::discover_airframe_roster`, `cs_formats::gamez::read_gamez_nodes`, `cs_formats::gamez::read_gamez_meshes`), plus the two PNGs the capture tests wrote through `cs_app::world::gpu_capture::capture_world_mesh`; validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass. The census artifact is checked against this report's own tree, install hash and content hash before it is referenced, so a stale file cannot be reported as this run's. The report's `unknowns` are this task's own blockers and are empty because the acceptance run passed; the product incompleteness this stage measured — the pilot's eye placement undeclared in every readable file, four of every twenty declared cockpit bindings resolving to container nodes rather than geometry, `CameraSetWindow`/`CameraSetHorizon`/`CameraSetHorizonXZ`/`CameraSetObjectHSETest` having no consumer in this camera contract, the `.zan`/`.zrd` camera clips still undecoded, and no shipped default key binding — is machine-readable in the referenced view-cockpit-coverage.json artifact and written out with its resolving task in docs/findings/2026-10-03-f21-d-original-view-controls-and-cockpit-coverage.md. `claim` is `implemented` only: what was measured is what the original's files declare, not what the original does when it runs. `candidate_tree` is the tree of the commit the suite ran on; the only later delta is this report's own copy under docs/findings/evidence/, whose bytes are that file.
